You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE TV_Channel (
    id TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    series_name TEXT,
    Country TEXT,
    Language TEXT,
    Content TEXT,
    Pixel_aspect_ratio_PAR TEXT,
    Hight_definition_TV TEXT,
    Pay_per_view_PPV TEXT,
    Package_Option TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id)
);

CREATE TABLE TV_series (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Episode TEXT,
    Air_Date TEXT,
    Rating TEXT,
    Share REAL,
    18_49_Rating_Share TEXT,
    Viewers_m TEXT,
    Weekly_Rank REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

CREATE TABLE Cartoon (
    id REAL   PRIMARY KEY,
    Title TEXT,
    Directed_by TEXT,
    Written_by TEXT,
    Original_air_date TEXT,
    Production_code REAL,
    Channel TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id),
    FOREIGN KEY (Channel) REFERENCES TV_Channel(id)
);

What kind of “popularity” do you want to analyze (ratings/share vs viewers vs weekly rank), and do you want it **by episode**, **by series/channel**, or **over time**?

Meanwhile, here are common SQL queries for TV series popularity using your schema.

### 1) Most popular episodes (by viewers)
```sql
SELECT
  s.Episode,
  s.Air_Date,
  s.Viewers_m,
  s.Rating,
  s.Share,
  s.Weekly_Rank,
  c.series_name AS channel_name
FROM TV_series s
LEFT JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
ORDER BY CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL) DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

### 2) Best average-performing channels (avg viewers + avg rating)
```sql
SELECT
  c.series_name AS channel_name,
  AVG(CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL)) AS avg_viewers_m,
  AVG(CAST(s.Rating AS REAL)) AS avg_rating,
  AVG(s.Share) AS avg_share,
  COUNT(*) AS episodes
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
GROUP BY c.id, c.series_name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY avg_viewers_m DESC;
```

### 3) Trend over time (monthly viewers, all channels or per channel)
**All channels:**
```sql
SELECT
  SUBSTR(s.Air_Date, 1, 7) AS month,
  AVG(CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL)) AS avg_viewers_m,
  AVG(CAST(s.Rating AS REAL)) AS avg_rating,
  COUNT(*) AS episodes
FROM TV_series s
GROUP BY SUBSTR(s.Air_Date, 1, 7)
ORDER BY month;
```

**Per channel:**
```sql
SELECT
  c.series_name AS channel_name,
  SUBSTR(s.Air_Date, 1, 7) AS month,
  AVG(CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL)) AS avg_viewers_m
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
GROUP BY c.series_name, SUBSTR(s.Air_Date, 1, 7)
ORDER BY c.series_name, month;
```

### 4) Episodes with the best weekly rank (rank 1 is best)
```sql
SELECT
  s.Episode,
  s.Air_Date,
  s.Weekly_Rank,
  s.Viewers_m,
  c.series_name AS channel_name
FROM TV_series s
LEFT JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
WHERE s.Weekly_Rank IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY s.Weekly_Rank ASC
LIMIT 20;
```

### 5) Compare popularity by country/language of channel
```sql
SELECT
  c.Country,
  c.Language,
  AVG(CAST(s.Viewers_m AS REAL)) AS avg_viewers_m,
  AVG(CAST(s.Rating AS REAL)) AS avg_rating,
  COUNT(*) AS episodes
FROM TV_series s
JOIN TV_Channel c ON c.id = s.Channel
GROUP BY c.Country, c.Language
ORDER BY avg_viewers_m DESC;
```

If you tell me:
1) which metric to prioritize (**Viewers_m**, **Rating**, **Share**, or **Weekly_Rank**), and  
2) whether you want results **per channel**, **per month**, or **top episodes**,  
I’ll tailor a single query (or dashboard-style set) to exactly what you need.
I'd like to see the minimum share of all TV series.

```sql
SELECT MIN(Share) AS min_share
FROM TV_series;
```
I also want to know the maximum share of all TV series.

```sql
SELECT MAX(Share) AS max_share
FROM TV_series;
```
